co_emerald_lake.blurb: Alpine bouldering on the talus around Emerald Lake, in Tyndall Gorge beneath Hallett Peak in Rocky Mountain National Park. The lake sits a bit over 10,000 feet and is reached by a hike of roughly 45 minutes up good trail from Bear Lake. Problems run from V0 up to V11, with a solid block of V5 to V9 testpieces, and several are traverses or sit starts. Whispers of Wisdom and Real Large are among the standouts. The setting is delicate: keep pads on rock instead of plants, take them home each day, and clear chalk and tick marks as you leave.

co_whiskey_rocks_west.blurb: Whiskey Rocks West is a granite outcrop in the Goose Creek country of the South Platte, a pocket known for knobby domes with superb friction and face climbing. Trad and sport routes share the rock in roughly equal numbers, along with a few boulder problems. Most lines fall around 5.9 and 5.10, with a smaller group pushing into the 5.12 and 5.13 range. Maker's Mark, Fireball and Winnie's Revenge are the trad favorites here. Approaches around Goose Creek tend to be short, and the wooded setting sits at roughly 8,000 feet.

co_piedra_river_east_side.blurb: The east wall of the Piedra River canyon, a short drive north of Pagosa Springs. The mix is bolted sport lines, a smaller number of trad routes, and a notable set of mixed climbs. Sport grades center on 5.10 through 5.12. It is a quiet, little-visited corner, so expect to find your own way and carry a stick clip. Parts of the lower face are loose, and poison ivy grows thick near the water in summer.
co_piedra_river_east_side.parking_note: Follow the gravel Piedra Road north out of Pagosa Springs and pull off about half a mile short of the river bridge. The crag lies down the bluff from the road.

co_high_wire_crag.blurb: High Wire Crag perches above the road in Clear Creek Canyon west of Golden, directly over the east end of Tunnel 2. It is mostly bolted face and slab climbing with a handful of trad lines, spanning 5.7 to low 5.13 and weighted toward the 5.10 to 5.12 range. Many consider it among the best moderate crags in the canyon, so weekends get crowded. Standouts include 5th of July, Road Warrior and Machine Gun Funk. The trail to the upper routes is loose; watch for rocks kicked down onto the base of 5th of July.
co_high_wire_crag.parking_note: Use the roadside pullouts along US 6 just short of the bridge near Tunnel 2; the north side is the easier choice.

co_overhang_area.blurb: The Overhang Area sits where the main trail meets the cliff band on North Table Mountain above Golden, which makes it one of the busiest stretches of the Golden Cliffs. Trad and sport routes appear in about equal numbers, from 5.7 to 5.12, with most lines between 5.8 and 5.11. Many climbs lean slightly past vertical but nothing is radically steep. The cliffs face south and west, so cool days are comfortable. Mr. Squirrel Places a Nut is the landmark line. Anchors are worn, so rappel or lower with your own carabiners, and watch for rattlesnakes in warm months.
co_overhang_area.parking_note: Two lots serve the mesa off Peery Parkway in Golden. Start in the lower one, which has a restroom and the trailhead sign; the upper lot only handles overflow.

co_mickey_mouse_wall.blurb: Mickey Mouse Wall is the best-known crag on the east side of Eldorado Mountain, just outside Eldorado Canyon, and the rock is good sandstone. Climbing is mostly traditional, with a few sport and mixed lines, in lengths up to about five pitches. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.13 with the bulk in the 5.10 to 5.11 range; Green Dihedral, Perversion and Captain Beyond are the moderate multi-pitch favorites. The approach is long and rough, and the trail beneath the wall is poor, so traffic stays light. Poison ivy is common; long pants help.

co_main_wall_5.blurb: The Main Wall is the most-climbed section of Ophir Wall, above the tiny town of Ophir about 15 miles south of Telluride, at over 9,000 feet. The climbing is old school and mostly traditional, with a few sport lines, on technical routes that can be runout and sometimes run to many pitches. Grades are concentrated at 5.9 and 5.10, with a few hard lines up to 5.13. Y-Crack, Black Primo and Hot Wee Wee are the classics here. Bring small gear and a steady head, and wear a helmet.

co_puff_s_lair.blurb: Puff's Lair is the crag you see from the road as you drive up to the Castle View area near Bailey, at roughly 8,300 feet. It has a north and a south face of short, high-quality routes, a blend of sport and trad with plenty of 5.10 to 5.12, plus boulder problems from V0 to V7 close by. Imagine Dragon, Corpse of a Cottonwood and The You You Are are the ones to try. The crag began as a top-rope spot and some anchors show the history, so look them over. A short walk from the lot gets you there.
co_puff_s_lair.parking_note: Leave the car at the Miller Gulch Trailhead lot, off the Wellington Lake road southeast of Bailey, rather than the one-car wide spot at the turnoff.
co_puff_s_lair.approach: Walk back along the access road from the lot, then bear into the trees toward the large boulder and follow the path uphill to the formation. The big roof marks the crag.

co_arch_rock_2.blurb: Arch Rock is a big granite dome rising some 500 feet from the South Platte River, about four miles up the Elevenmile Canyon road. Trad climbs outnumber sport lines, with a mix of one- and two-pitch routes mostly in the 5.5 to 5.9 range and a few reaching 5.11. Bolted routes sit between trad lines, with long runouts on easier ground. The Staircase, Hollow Flake and Arch Rock Route are the moderate classics. Expect shade in the morning and sun in the afternoon, and plan to descend gullies on the south side of the dome.
co_arch_rock_2.parking_note: Pull in on the west side of the road behind the big boulder below the dome, or use the small pullout upstream on the east side. If you reach the footbridge lot or a tunnel, you have gone too far.

co_brown_town.blurb: Brown Town is the main sector of Down Under, a cluster of formations north of Westcreek on the east side of Thunder Butte, in the South Platte. The rock is steep, sunny, featured granite in the forest, and the climbing is technical face work, mostly bolted with a number of trad lines. Almost everything falls between 5.9 and 5.12, with 5.10 to 5.12 the heart of it. Bushworld, Black Opal and Give It Heaps are stand-out sport lines. Most walls face south, so late spring afternoons and crisp fall days suit it best; snow can make the hike hard.
co_brown_town.approach: A steady uphill hike of about 1.1 miles gains roughly 1,000 feet. Allow most of an hour the first time. Cell service is nearly absent, so save the map beforehand.
